scope.flow: injectSweepAndCall on TrailsRouter intended for delegatecall execution from a wallet/shim but callable directly on the router
scope.environment: TrailsRouter contract with DelegatecallGuard modifier available

statements.text: The router is intended to be used via delegatecall from a smart wallet or shim contract, so address(this) resolves to the wallet/shim and _getSelfBalance tracks the wallet's balances.
A caller invokes injectSweepAndCall directly on the router contract as a normal external call.
injectSweepAndCall is declared as a normal external function without any onlyDelegatecall or equivalent restriction, so direct external calls on the router are allowed.

When called directly on the router, injectSweepAndCall transfers tokens from msg.sender into address(this) (the router) and subsequent internal logic uses the router's own balance via _getSelfBalance / address(this), turning the stateless router into a stateful asset custodian.
injectSweepAndCall must be restricted to delegatecall-only execution, e.g. via the onlyDelegatecall modifier, so it cannot execute as a direct external call on the router.
The router must remain pure logic with no long-term funds; all balances belong to the calling wallet, so direct calls must not cause the router to accumulate and control user funds.
Users may unknowingly send funds to ROUTER expecting a stateless routing behavior.
Funds remain in ROUTER without a clear path to recovery.
the attacker can drain these accumulated balances.

ambiguities: Report does not state whether the caller is authorized or permissionless for the direct call; only that the function is fully callable on the router implementation.
No explicit numeric amounts, token identities, or target configuration are given for the direct-call scenario.
The link between accumulated router balances and the prior injectAndCall drain bug is described as a separate prior finding, not established within this scenario.
